findings.where: First screen (hero) at desktop and phone, and the whole page: no contact anywhere
findings.fault: There is no way to reach Mark anywhere on the page. The hero has the name, the line, the photo and three nav links, but no email address and no contact link. The parts map lists no mailto or contact target, and the nav has no 'Contact'. The palette card says the pad yellow is for 'the address strip' and the texture card draws that strip at the foot of the sheet, but the hero doesn't have it.
findings.who_objects: The bank official who has just decided Mark might be the right PPP-law advisor. They have nowhere to write and would have to search elsewhere for an address. The founder would object too: the brief requires one action with the address shown on the first screen, and it is the site's one action (brand sheet §1; first-visit trust item 7).

findings.where: Motion sketch panel, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The motion panel sits on a saturated lavender fill. That hue is in no palette card and in neither house colour. It is the loudest block on the page, and in the overview the eye lands on it right after the portrait. It breaks the direction's 'one soft ground, house blue and grey as the only ink' and makes the house blue link sit on purple.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark. The brief builds every tile in or around #0070C0 and #404040 with at most one pale yellow memory. A lilac block reads as off-brand and slightly playful, not as counsel's paper.

findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and 'Download', and the heavy article title
findings.fault: The subheads use a heavy, wide grotesque that is neither of the two declared faces. The type-pair card says subheads are Newsreader 500. Next to the light serif voice they look blunt and techy, and the title's heavy weight also jumps far above the hero's light 300. The page shows three type voices where the tile promises two.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for serious type and nothing 'in-your-face techy'. Angélique would also object: she copies the specimen when adding articles and would pick up a face the system doesn't name.

findings.where: First screen and article specimen: where the pad yellow is used
findings.fault: The direction's one borrowed memory, the pale legal-pad yellow behind the contact panel or one quotation, is never actually used. It appears only as a swatch and a texture diagram. With it gone, the first screen is an ivory page with a hairline frame and a portrait, a look any consultancy could own.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who wanted the legal pad saved 'with careful intention'. Mark leaned toward the legal pad 'given my legal background'. Without the yellow, v1 cannot be judged against the other tiles as Counsel's paper.

findings.where: First screen: the line under the name and the supporting paragraph
findings.fault: Nothing on the first screen says where Mark is based or which regions he works in. The only credential is 'Formerly Lead Lawyer, PPP Group, World Bank', and no work or date sits near it.
findings.who_objects: A multilateral-bank official shortlisting advisors against terms of reference, who judges relevant experience by region and project kind. They have to dig to learn whether he has worked in their region (first-visit trust items 3 and 6).

findings.where: Motion sketch table at phone width
findings.fault: The four-column timing table is kept at 390 px. The Element column wraps to one or two words a line ('Mark's / line / settles: / opacity / 0 to 1 …'), so the rows are tall, ragged and hard to read.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who reviews tiles on a phone too and would struggle to read the timing. It also makes the motion spec look careless.

findings.fault: Each swatch is a different shape: a hairline rectangle, a rounded rectangle, an ellipse, and a rectangle with a blue border. The shapes mean nothing, so they look like a mistake. The blue-bordered yellow also looks like a selected option.
findings.who_objects: The founder, comparing tiles. A tile that sells 'refined, never childish' reads as unfinished when its own colour card is inconsistent.

findings.where: Article specimen: the Download row at desktop
findings.fault: The 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' line is pushed to the far right, a wide gap away from the title it describes. It reads as a separate item rather than the link's own details.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning the downloads, who has to match the details to the title across the gap. This gets worse once the list has several rows.

findings.where: Article specimen title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'
findings.fault: The title uses a straight typewriter apostrophe, while the body and subhead use curly quotes. At display size the mismatch is obvious.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader and the founder. A legal-journal look depends on correct typesetting, and a straight quote at 90 px undercuts it.
